name: Question 19
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x(2xy+3y),\,y(1)=1
$$

Use the modified Euler method with one step to approximate $y(2).$

$y(2)≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the modified Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Predictor} & : & Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx, \\ \text{Corrector} & : & Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})\cdot Δx,\end{aligned}
$$

where ${y}_{p}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})$ is the initially predicted slope at the predicted new point $({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})=(x+Δx,y+Δ{y}_{p}).$

Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=2,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=2-1=1.
$$

First, we add the initial condition data to a table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Now, we compute the value of ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =x(2xy+3y) \\  & =1(2\cdot 1\cdot 1+3\cdot 1) \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $5$ |  |  |  |  |

Next, we compute $Δ{y}_{p}$ using the predictor equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =5\cdot 1 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $5$ | $5$ |  |  |  |

The coordinates of the initially predicted new point given by the predictor equation are

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=1+1=2, \\ {y}_{p} & =y+Δ{y}_{p}=1+5=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add the second value to the table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $5$ | $5$ | $6$ |  |  |

So, the predicted slope at this point is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ={x}_{\text{new}}(2{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{p}+3{y}_{p}) \\  & =2(2\cdot 2\cdot 6+3\cdot 6) \\  & =84.\end{aligned}
$$

We can add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $5$ | $5$ | $6$ | $84$ |  |

Finally, we compute $Δy$ using the corrector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{p}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(5+84)\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 89 \\  & =\frac{89}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $5$ | $5$ | $6$ | $84$ | $\frac{89}{2}$ |

The value of $x$ in the next row is ${x}_{\text{new}}=2.$ To get the value of $y$ in the next row, we add $Δy$ to $y:$

$$
{y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy=1+\frac{89}{2}=\frac{2}{2}+\frac{89}{2}=\frac{91}{2}.
$$

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $1$ | $5$ | $5$ | $6$ | $84$ | $\frac{89}{2}$ |
| $2$ | $\frac{91}{2}$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(2)≈\frac{91}{2}.$

y(2)≈
912​

EXPLANATION

For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y0=y(x0), the modified Euler method with step size Δx is given by Predictor:Δyp=y′⋅Δx,Corrector:Δy=12(y′+yp′)⋅Δx, where yp′=f(xnew,yp) is the initially predicted slope at the predicted new point (xnew,yp)=(x+Δx,y+Δyp).

Since we want to find the value of y at x=2, we will use a step size of Δx=2−1=1.

First, we add the initial condition data to a table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 1

Now, we compute the value of y′ according to the given rule:

y′=x(2xy+3y)=1(2⋅1⋅1+3⋅1)=5

So, we add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 1 5

Next, we compute Δyp using the predictor equation:

Δyp=y′⋅Δx=5⋅1=5

We add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 1 5 5

The coordinates of the initially predicted new point given by the predictor equation are

xnew=x+Δx=1+1=2,yp=y+Δyp=1+5=6.

Let's add the second value to the table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 1 5 5 6

So, the predicted slope at this point is yp′=xnew(2xnewyp+3yp)=2(2⋅2⋅6+3⋅6)=84.

We can add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 1 5 5 6 84

Finally, we compute Δy using the corrector equation:

Δy=12(y′+yp′)⋅Δx=12(5+84)⋅1=12⋅89=892

We add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 1 5 5 6 84 892

The value of x in the next row is xnew=2. To get the value of y in the next row, we add Δy to y: ynew=y+Δy=1+892=22+892=912.

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 1 5 5 6 84 892
2 912

Therefore, we conclude that y(2)≈912.
